title: NPCWander.cs
summary: Walks an NPC between waypoints around the house. It stands still while the player is close enough to talk and during any conversation.

notes.match: public enum Pattern { Loop, PingPong, Random }
notes.text: Loop: 1,2,3,1,2,3. PingPong: 1,2,3,2,1. Random: any point next, so every pair of points needs a clear straight line.
Plain scene objects (under 'NPC Waypoints'). Move, add or delete them in the Hierarchy — no code changes.
The NPC turns on the spot first and only starts walking once it faces within this many degrees of the target, so it never slides sideways.
A random rest between the two numbers at each waypoint.
Stands still while the player is inside the NPC's interaction radius, so the NPC doesn't walk away mid-approach.
A kinematic Rigidbody lets the NPC move every frame without Unity rebuilding the static physics world.
Kinematic: moved by script only. The NPC's own collider still blocks the player.
Starts at whichever waypoint is nearest where the NPC was placed.

notes.match: if (NPCInteractionManager.DialogueActive) { SetWalking(false); return; } // the conversation system owns rotation while talking
notes.text: While any conversation is open, this script does nothing so it doesn't fight the manager turning the NPC toward the player.
Reuses the NPC's own interaction radius, so 'close enough to press F' and 'stands still' are always the same distance.
Always turn toward the target; the returned angle decides whether to move yet.
Moves in 3D toward the waypoint, so a rug's few centimetres of height are followed smoothly.
Reverses direction at either end of the list.
Draws the route in the Scene view when the NPC is selected: spheres at the waypoints and lines between them.
